K102.notes: Read from the installed 2.0.1 binary, which carries full C++ symbols; the plugin publishes no source. Two pitch faults. The primary oscillator's frequency is 261.6256 times two to the power of (knob minus twelve plus twelve times the pitch voltage) over twelve (K102::process, 0x1240 to 0x12c0), so the knob's own tooltip, which is configured with a semitone display base against 261.6256, reads exactly one octave above the note that is sounding. And the secondary oscillator in its Detune setting adds the pitch voltage to a semitone count without multiplying by twelve (0x12f4), so it rises one semitone per volt where the primary rises an octave; the two therefore part company as soon as a keyboard is patched. In the Free setting the secondary is instead a ratio of the primary's frequency, clamped to plus or minus twenty-four semitones. Both oscillator frequencies are finally clamped between 0.1Hz and 20000Hz. The pitch input is clamped to 0 to 5V before anything is done with it. The output passes through a sixteen-bit quantiser with a rand()-based dither term added (0x1b64 to 0x1bc0) before the plus or minus 5V clamp. The switch choices are the maker's own strings: LFO Mode is Pitch A/B, Pitch B and Alpha; LFO Waveform is Square/Random, Up/Down and Triangle/Sine; LFO Bank is Bank A (Sq/Up/Tri) and Bank B (Rnd/Down/Sin); Method is Phase, Multiply and Fade; Sync is Off and On; OSC B Mode is Free and Detune; OSC B Bank Copy is Sine to Sawtooth and Copy from A. Index order is not panel order for the inputs: the middle jack is input three, the modulation one.

K104.notes: Read from the installed 2.0.1 binary. Two findings. The polarity switch is configured with the choices Positive and Negative at values 0 and 1, and the code selects one minus the envelope when the parameter is BELOW 0.5 (K104::process, 0x8a70) - so the choice named Positive, which is also the default, is the one that turns the envelope upside down. And the control CV jack is not an offset but a multiplier on the attack, decay and release parameters: quantizeCV maps the voltage to voltage times 0.05 plus 0.5, clamped to 0 to 1 and quantised to 256 steps, and that factor multiplies all three times before they reach the envelope (0x8a48 to 0x8a54). An unpatched jack reads 0V, which gives a factor of one half, so the module's real times are half the times its own tooltips display, and only at plus 10V do the two agree. The sustain parameter is not scaled. The times themselves are 0.001 seconds times 10000 to the power of the parameter, so 1ms to 10 seconds. The curve control is an exponent of two to the power of one minus twice the parameter (K104::getShapedEnvelope, 0x8944), giving a squared curve at zero, a straight line at one half and a square root at one.

K108.notes: Read from the installed 2.0.1 binary. The module carries a ninth parameter, Volume, configured 0 to 1 with a default of 0.8 - and it has no ParamWidget on the panel and is never read in process, so it can be neither turned nor heard. It gets no line here because no click can reach it. Both filter type switches default to VCA, the middle of their three settings, so a freshly placed K108 filters nothing. The cutoff parameters are configured with a display base of 1000 and a multiplier of 20, which is 20Hz to 20000Hz; a cutoff CV of one volt moves the parameter a tenth of its travel, and a tenth of three decades is 0.997 of an octave, so those jacks are within a third of a per cent of 1V per octave and are coloured as pitch. The resonance CV jack is shared: one voltage is added to BOTH filters' resonance parameters. Process returns 0V immediately when the audio input has no cable (0xb1b8). The filter models are named Ladder and Biquad in configSwitch, at values 0 and 1; the panel prints them in Japanese under the English heading FILTER I TYPE, while the low pass, high pass and VCA switch is the one the maker's tooltip calls Filter A Type.
